summary: This program reworks Frederick's RobotPet class into a family of pets: RobotCat, RobotBird, and RobotDog each inherit RobotPet's setup and battery protection, and each adds its own sound method. One of each is created and asked to speak.

lines.code: self.battery = battery  # uses the property setter for validation
lines.text: Assigning to self.battery inside __init__ goes through the property setter rather than storing the number directly, so a pet cannot be born with an impossible battery level. Every subclass gets this checking for free.
The parent class in parentheses is what makes RobotCat a subclass: it inherits the __init__ and the battery property from RobotPet without repeating a line of them.
Each subclass adds only what makes it different. meow belongs to cats alone, so a RobotBird has no meow and calling one would be an error.
The method reaches self.name, an attribute the parent's __init__ set, showing that inherited attributes are fully available inside a subclass's own methods.
RobotCat defines no __init__ of its own, so Python uses the one it inherited, which is why the three arguments are still name, battery, and mood.
Each object answers with its own species' sound method, which is the payoff of inheritance: shared behaviour lives in one place, and only the differences are written three times.
